The Inner Journey: Story-Led Sound Bath
Across cultures and throughout history, stories have guided people inward, offering wisdom, comfort, and connection. This immersive sound bath blends ancient poetic narratives with the soothing sounds of harmonium, flutes, crystal bowls, and gentle voice to create a space of stillness, reflection, and deep listening.
Mats, blankets and cushions are provided but feel free to bring anything else to aid your comfort.
Meet Smita, your host:
From a young age, Smita was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.
Meet Alexandra, your host:
Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

name: The Adam Portraiture Award 2026: Artists Talk
venue: 60 Lady Elizabeth Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Join us for a kōrero facilitated by New Zealand Portrait Gallery Director Brian Wood, featuring three of this year’s Te Whanganui-a-Tara–based Adam Portraiture Award finalists: Sacha Lees, Benjamin Dellabarca, and Emma Hercus.
Sacha Lees is a Pōneke-based artist. Her work has been shown in solo and group exhibitions, most recently at the Dowse Art Museum. Sacha won the 2020 Adam Portraiture Award, was Highly Commended for her work in 2022, and won the People’s Choice Award in 2022. She was commissioned to paint King Charles III in 2025. Sacha studied drawing in Florence, Italy, and earned First Class Honours in MFA at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa | Massey University in 2024. Her paintings are held in public and private collections across Aotearoa.
Emma Hercus is a Plimmerton based painter. She has a diploma in creativity from The Learning connection and is studying towards a masters in fine art from Whitecliffe art school. Her latest solo exhibition was at Twenty Six Gallery in 2026.
Born in Wellington in 2003, Ben Dellabarca began drawing at an early age and promptly found his love for oil painting. Instead of pursuing the conventional path of formal art education, Ben sought out mentorships and communities, studying at the Wellington school of drawing followed by attending the Nerdrum school in Larkvik, Norway. id: SCUBA: subterranean critters – understanding biodiversity Aotearoa--41.267300, 174.759000-Facebook
name: SCUBA: subterranean critters – understanding biodiversity Aotearoa
long_description:
Join Julia Kasper, Lead Curator Invertebrates at Te Papa, as she talks about Subterranean ecosystems - some of the least explored habitats on Earth. Globally, scientific knowledge of cave and groundwater invertebrates remains fragmentary, with most regions having only sporadic surveys or taxonomic treatments. Many cave systems host highly specialised faunal assemblages - troglobionts, stygofauna, and other obligate subterranean species - that often display extreme adaptations such as reduced pigmentation, elongated appendages, or complete loss of eyes.
The Subterranean Critters: Understanding cave Biodiversity in Aotearoa (SCUBA) project brings together the expertise of a wide range of researchers and cavers to better understand the biodiversity and ecology of faunal communities in caves in Aotearoa New Zealand.
Novel sample collection, combined with reviews of the literature and presently available natural history collection holdings, will enable species discovery and improved understanding of the distribution and conservation status of cave taxa, as well as the abiotic factors that influence their distribution, ecology, and abundance.

Located in Tāne Whakapiripiri, Ōtari Visitor Centre. Gold coin donation. No need to book, just turn up!
This seminar is part of the Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush Trust’s annual seminar series. This year, they are on the first Tuesday of the month, March – November, to celebrate 100 years of Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush.
Ōtari 100: Celebrating 100 years of native plants, conservation, and community. 1926-2026.

Come join us for a morning of inspiration and connection with This gathering's focus is the Season of Creation 2026 theme: Living Water inspired by Ezekiel 47:1–12. Together we'll reflect on water as a gift from God and our calling to care for the waterways and ecosystems that sustain our communities. Drawing on Te Ao Māori understanding of wai as a taonga, we'll explore our relationship with water not simply as a resource to be used, but as a living gift to be respected, cared for, and protected.
We're delighted to have two excellent presenters joining us:
Ben Fountain, a water engineer with Awa Environmental, will help us understand our relationship with local waterways, where Wellington's water comes from, the challenges facing our region, and the practical ways churches can help protect the health of local waterways.
Anna Baird will share the inspiring story of how her church, The Tribe in Masterton, has cared for the Awatotara Stream that runs alongside their church. What was once a neglected drain is becoming a place where native plants and wildlife are returning—a powerful example of faithful local action making a tangible difference. Anna will share what they've learned along the way and what other churches can take inspiration from.
There'll also be plenty of opportunity to ask questions, share what's happening in your own church, learn from others across the Wellington region, and enjoy coffee, tea and, of course, cake! If you're able, come a little earlier and go for a walk along Plimmerton Beach at 9:00am before the gathering begins. long_description:
Pyramid Club is excited to present master drummer Riki Pirihi, in a performance residency over 2 nights and an afternoon participatory Conduction workshop.
Riki Pirihi (Ngāti Wai, Patuharakeke, Ngāti Māhanga) is one of the most important musicians of his generation in Aotearoa. As a drummer he has been the rhythmic force behind a huge number of bands and A-list mucisians including Trinity Roots, Fat Freddy's Drop, Connan Mockasin, Anika Moa, Jonathan Crayford, Crowded House, Recloose, Ladi6, Orchestra of Spheres and Dave Dobbyn to name but a few. Working solo under Cave Circles, Riki is constantly reinventing his music, from experimental electronics to taonga pūoro.
Recently Riki completed a Doctor of Musical Arts degree centred on the cultivation of a unique lexicon termed Rangatuone, which intertwines the principles of Conduction (improvised conducting) with expressive signs and gestures, tailored specifically for the composition and performance of taonga pūoro alongside Western instruments.
Through all this astonishing variety of musical settings, Riki's foundation has always been in improvisation, and it's with pleasure that we welcome him home to Pyramid Club for two nights of improvised collaborations with a diverse lineup of artists from Wellington's creative music family.
Riki will play solo, duo, trio and quartet sets on both the Friday and Saturday night concerts, and will lead a participatory conduction workshop on Saturday afternoon.

Whether you have a fresh idea for next year's fringe circuit, or an existing show planning its next steps- we'll cover everything you need to know with plenty of time for tailored feedback and advice.

- Assembling the right team, contracting and looking after your people.

name: Into the West: A Choral Journey of Voice, Land, and Connection

long_description:
For its second concert of 2026, Supertonic is thrilled to be joining forces with the renowned Oregon Chorale of Portland for Into the West: A Choral Journey of Voice, Land and Connection. This will be the Supertonic’s first international collaboration with another choir in its twelve-year history. The one-night-only concert, to be presented on Saturday 1 August at St Andrew’s on the Terrace, will see both choirs perform individual sets before joining forces to bring the evening to a memorable close.
Into the West invites audiences on a musical journey celebrating renewal, discovery, and the landscapes—both real and imagined—that shape our sense of home. Drawing inspiration from the Pacific horizon, the programme weaves together New Zealand and Māori folk songs, works by Pacific Northwest composers, global choral favourites, and film-inspired pieces. The result is a concert rich in storytelling and atmosphere, uniting contemporary voices and timeless traditions in a spirit of connection and exploration.
Founded in 1985, the Oregon Chorale is an auditioned community choir based near Portland, Oregon, in the Pacific Northwest of the United States, and is led by Artistic Director Jason Sabino. Guided by its mission to inspire and connect communities through exceptional choral performances and meaningful educational outreach, the Chorale performs a wide range of repertoire, from classical masterworks to contemporary works by living composers.
Supertonic shares Oregon Chorale’s enthusiasm for varied repertoire, striving to push the boundaries of what choral music can be. Since the choir was formed in 2014, it has performed concerts spanning the entire musical spectrum, from Vaughan Williams’ Mass in G Minor, Vivaldi’s Gloria, and Fauré’s Requiem to pop and rock spectaculars celebrating Fleetwood Mac, David Bowie, Elton John, and Queen. For this concert, Supertonic will be directed by Isaac Stone, who is excited to be working with the choir again for the first time since the smash-hit It’s All Coming Back in November 2024.

name: Riki Pirihi - Conduction Workshop
venue: Fors, 298 Taranaki St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
As part of his 2-night performance residency, Pyramid Club is excited to present master drummer Riki Pirihi in an afternoon participatory Conduction workshop. Bring an instrument! Koha entry!
For this workshop Riki invites anyone to participate. Bring an instrument or your voice. No previous experience necessary. Riki will lead the workshop ensemble in an improvised Conduction session using his unique Rangatuone method, where expressive signs and gestures form the basis of a collaborative, improvised piece.
Riki Pirihi (Ngāti Wai, Patuharakeke, Ngāti Māhanga) is one of the most important musicians of his generation in Aotearoa. As a drummer he has been the rhythmic force behind a huge number of bands and A-list mucisians including Trinity Roots, Fat Freddy's Drop, Connan Mockasin, Anika Moa, Jonathan Crayford, Crowded House, Recloose, Ladi6, Orchestra of Spheres and Dave Dobbyn to name but a few. Working solo under Cave Circles, Riki is constantly reinventing his music, from experimental electronics to taonga pūoro.
Recently Riki completed a Doctor of Musical Arts degree centred on the cultivation of a unique musical language, Rangatuone, which intertwines the principles of Conduction (improvised conducting) with expressive signs and gestures, tailored specifically for the composition and performance of taonga pūoro alongside Western instruments.
